answer: Agent economies can blunt sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a refundable bond before it can vote or claim rewards. Each agent locks a stake that rises with the number of identities it controls, so spinning up a thousand fake workers costs a thousand bonds. Peers also cross-check work, and a tide of mismatched results triggers slashing of the bonded stake. A zenith of trust is reached only after sustained honest output, while a ferrous wall of collateral makes cheap identity farms uneconomic.
